newsitem.title: UK: ASDA outlines spending as H1 profits rise.
newsitem.headline: ASDA outlines spending as H1 profits rise.

text.p: British supermarket group ASDA Plc said it expected capital expenditure for the full year to be around 500 million pounds ($832.9 million) and would open seven stores, with debt levels increasing marginally from 15 percent at the half year end.
It said in a statement that pretax profits for the half year were 160.1 million pounds, up 15.8 percent, and paid out an interim dividend of 0.81 pence per share, up 12.5 percent.

ASDA, which focuses on low prices and is the only one of the big four supermarkets not to have launched a loyalty card nationwide, saw first-half sales from existing stores jump 10.2 percent and increased its market share to 10.6 percent.
"Keeping it simple has been the key to our success. These results show we are on course to deliver...our (strategy) programme for 1998," chairman Archie Norman said in a statement.
The company said that own-brand goods now accounted for 35 percent of total sales, adding it was "well on our way to achieving our...objective of 40 percent ASDA brand penetration by 1998".
ASDA said that its aim to be lowest on price had been achieved "with only a modest investment in our gross margin", as it moved to cut operating and distribution costs.
